# Behavior-preserving refactor

Read before renaming, moving, extracting, or reshaping code whose external behavior should remain the
same.

1. Define the behavior and compatibility surface to preserve. Add characterization tests where
   existing tests do not pin it.
2. Map callers, configuration, serialization, reflection, scripts, docs, and cross-language consumers;
   search the whole repository and inspect relevant history before deleting an odd branch.
3. Use language/tooling-aware rename/extract operations where possible. Work in small reviewable
   steps and keep the focused suite green.
4. Separate behavior changes from mechanical changes in the review evidence. They may share a commit
   only when the repository workflow requires it and the diff remains independently understandable.
5. If a shared contract must change, expand → migrate every consumer → contract. Use a rollout flag
   when deployment and behavior rollback must be independent.

A changed test is a signal to explain, not automatic proof of a product behavior change: fixtures,
test APIs, or obsolete implementation assertions may legitimately change. Preserve observable tests;
call out any intentional contract change explicitly.

Done means the preserved behavior is covered, all known consumers use a supported path, deprecations
and compatibility windows are recorded, and the regression suite has fresh evidence. Report anything
not searched, migrated, or verified.
